what_it_is: IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre) is the single-window, autonomous promotion-and-authorisation agency under India's Department of Space, established by the Government of India in June 2020. It authorises and supervises space activities of non-governmental entities - including building launch vehicles and satellites and providing space-based services - and interfaces between ISRO and private players. It also maintains public authorisation registries for entities using Indian orbital slots and capacity.
india_angle: IN-SPACe is the regulatory gateway for every private Indian space company in this atlas - its authorisations and promotion schemes (seed support, design-lab access, transfer of ISRO technology) shape who can build, launch and operate. Public IN-SPACe authorisation listings are a primary, verifiable evidence source for private space activity in India.
intelligence_assessment: As a government body, IN-SPACe's own publications constitute official evidence for the sector. The atlas listing for IN-SPACe was a dead link at crawl time; this dossier restores the entity with primary sources. Watch authorisation decisions and norms revisions - they move the commercial position of every dossier in the space vertical.

faq.a: India's single-window agency under the Department of Space, set up in June 2020 to promote, authorise and supervise space activities of non-governmental entities.
The Government of India established IN-SPACe on 24 June 2020.

faq.q: How does IN-SPACe differ from ISRO?
faq.a: ISRO is the space agency; IN-SPACe authorises and promotes private-sector space activity and interfaces between ISRO and non-governmental entities.
